narr: The remnants from tropical system Beryl moved across northeast Illinois on July 9th. Many areas along and east of Interstate 57 received 2 to 3 inches with locally higher amounts. The highest rainfall amount reported was 3.93 inches in St. Anne in Kankakee County. Despite these rainfall amounts, no significant flooding was reported.||Isolated thunderstorms developed over the far south side of Chicago and southern Cook County during the mid afternoon of July 9th. A narrow corridor of 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in these areas, producing localized flash flooding.
ev: Multiple reports of street flooding were received from Blue Island and Calumet Park as well as the Pullman and Hegewisch neighborhoods of Chicago. Water rescues of stranded motorists were reported in the vicinity of 130th Street and Stoney Island Avenue. Multiple basements were flooded in the West Pullman neighborhood and a few basements were flooded in the Hegewisch neighborhood. A public transportation bus was stuck in flood waters in Riverdale and needed to be towed. Water entered an industrial building northeast of Dolton and water entered a second industrial building near the Hegewisch neighborhood, which needed to be evacuated.
